questions.title: Fibonacci Term
questions.description:
The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long fib(int n)

It must return the n-th Fibonacci number with F(0) = 0, F(1) = 1 and F(n) = F(n-1) + F(n-2). Build the answer bottom-up (tabulation) — naive recursion would recompute far too much.

Input Format:
Line 1: n.

Output Format:
One line with F(n).

Constraints:
0 <= n <= 40

questions.title: Climbing Stairs Ways
questions.description:
The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long climb_ways(int n)

A staircase has n steps; from a step you may climb 1 or 2 stairs at a time. Count the DISTINCT ways to reach the top: ways(1) = 1, ways(2) = 2, ways(n) = ways(n-1) + ways(n-2). Use tabulation.

Input Format:
Line 1: n.

Output Format:
One line with the number of ways.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 40

questions.title: Domino Tiling Count
questions.description:
The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long tile_ways(int n)

A 2 x n board must be tiled with 2 x 1 dominoes (placed vertically or horizontally). The count satisfies the same recurrence as climbing stairs: tile_ways(1) = 1, tile_ways(2) = 2, tile_ways(n) = tile_ways(n-1) + tile_ways(n-2). Fill a table bottom-up.

Input Format:
Line 1: n.

Output Format:
One line with the number of tilings.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 40

questions.title: Knapsack Max Value
questions.description:
The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int knapsack_max(int n, int weight[], int value[], int W)

Classic 0/1 knapsack: each item is taken whole or not at all; total weight must not exceed W; maximise total value. Fill a 1-D dp table of size W+1, iterating weights backwards so each item is used at most once, and return dp[W].

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n item weights. Line 3: n item values. Line 4: capacity W.

Output Format:
One line with the maximum value.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50, 1 <= weight[i] <= 100, 1 <= value[i] <= 1000, 1 <= W <= 500

questions.title: LCS Length
questions.description:
The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int lcs_length(char a[], char b[])

It must return the length of the LONGEST COMMON SUBSEQUENCE of the two strings (characters in order, not necessarily contiguous). Fill the classic (len(a)+1) x (len(b)+1) dp table: equal characters extend the diagonal by 1, otherwise take the better of dropping one character.

Input Format:
Line 1: string a. Line 2: string b (both without spaces).

Output Format:
One line with the LCS length.

Constraints:
1 <= |a|, |b| <= 50, strings use letters/digits only

questions.title: Subset Sum Exists
questions.description:
The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int subset_sum_exists(int n, int a[], int target)

It must return 1 when SOME subset of the n numbers sums exactly to target, else 0. Fill a boolean dp table over sums 0..target: dp[0] = 1 and, processing each number, mark dp[s] reachable when dp[s - a[i]] was reachable (iterate s downwards so each number is used once).

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n numbers. Line 3: target.

Output Format:
One line with 1 or 0.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 20, 1 <= a[i] <= 100, 1 <= target <= 2000

questions.title: Rabbit Pair Growth
questions.description:
A farm starts with 1 rabbit pair. Every month each adult pair produces one new pair, and a new pair needs one month to mature — the colony follows the Fibonacci sequence: month 1 and 2 have 1 pair, month n has pairs(n-1) + pairs(n-2). Report the colony size after n months.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long rabbit_pairs(int months)

It must return the number of pairs after the given months (memoize or tabulate; the value exceeds int for larger months).

Input Format:
Line 1: months.

Output Format:
One line with the number of rabbit pairs.

Constraints:
1 <= months <= 60

questions.title: Tower Staircase Routes
questions.description:
A tower staircase has n steps (climb 1 or 2 at a time), but one step is under repair and must NOT be stepped on. Count the routes that avoid the broken step: ways[0] = 1, a broken step has 0 routes, any other step sums the routes of the previous two.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long safe_routes(int n, int broken)

It must fill the ways table with the broken step pinned to 0 and return ways[n] (0 when the top itself is broken).

Input Format:
Line 1: n and broken (1 <= broken <= n).

Output Format:
One line with the number of safe routes.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 40, 1 <= broken <= n

questions.title: Campus Fund Allocation
questions.description:
A student council splits a fixed budget among independent projects: project i costs cost[i] and delivers impact[i]; each project is funded fully or not at all. Maximise the total impact within the budget — a 0/1 knapsack over the projects.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int allocate_funds(int n, int cost[], int impact[], int budget)

It must fill a 1-D dp table over amounts 0..budget (iterate budgets downwards so each project is funded at most once) and return dp[budget].

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n project costs. Line 3: n impact values. Line 4: budget.

Output Format:
One line with the maximum total impact.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50, 1 <= cost[i] <= 1000, 1 <= impact[i] <= 1000, 1 <= budget <= 5000

questions.title: Shared Subsequence Traits
questions.description:
Two DNA samples share traits measured as their LONGEST COMMON SUBSEQUENCE: characters appearing in both strings in the same order, not necessarily adjacent. Report the shared trait length.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int common_traits(char a[], char b[])

It must build the LCS dp table over the two strings and return dp[|a|][|b|].

Input Format:
Line 1: string a. Line 2: string b (both without spaces).

Output Format:
One line with the LCS length.

Constraints:
1 <= |a|, |b| <= 60, strings use letters/digits only

questions.title: Vendor Coin Change DP
questions.description:
A vending machine stocks arbitrary coin denominations (unlimited copies of each) and must dispense exact change with the FEWEST coins — greedy by value does NOT work for arbitrary denominations, so build a bottom-up dp table: dp[0] = 0 and dp[s] = 1 + min over coins of dp[s - coin]. Return the minimum coin count, or -1 when the amount cannot be formed.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int min_coins_dp(int n, int coins[], int amount)

It must fill a dp table of size amount+1 (mark unreachable sums with amount+1) and return dp[amount], or -1 when dp[amount] is still unreachable.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n coin denominations. Line 3: amount.

Output Format:
One line with the minimum number of coins, or -1.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 20, 1 <= coins[i] <= 1000, 1 <= amount <= 10000

questions.title: Night Watch Loot
questions.description:
A thief cases a row of houses; robbing two ADJACENT houses trips the alarm, so the chosen houses must be non-adjacent. Maximise the total loot with a rolling two-state dp (best up to the previous house vs best up to two houses back plus the current loot) — the O(1) memory formulation.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int max_loot(int val[], int n)

It must sweep the houses keeping prev1 (best ending at/just before the previous house) and prev2 (two back), computing best = max(prev1, prev2 + val[i]), and return the final best.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n house loot values.

Output Format:
One line with the maximum loot.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 0 <= val[i] <= 10000

questions.title: Coin Combination Tallies
questions.description:
Count (not minimise!) the number of DISTINCT WAYS to form an amount with unlimited copies of each coin, where the order of coins does not matter (2+1 and 1+2 are the same combination). The classic trick: iterate the COINS in the outer loop so combinations are counted once each — dp[a] += dp[a - coin].

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long count_ways(int n, int coins[], int amount)

It must fill a long long dp table (dp[0] = 1) with coins in the outer loop and return dp[amount].

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n coin denominations. Line 3: amount.

Output Format:
One line with the number of combinations.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 20, 1 <= coins[i] <= 1000, 1 <= amount <= 500

questions.title: Palindrome Subsequence Length
questions.description:
A puzzle app scores a string by its LONGEST PALINDROMIC SUBSEQUENCE — the longest sequence read the same forwards and backwards when characters are picked in order. This equals the LCS of the string with its reverse, or can be solved directly over intervals: dp[i][j] is the LPS length inside s[i..j].

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int lps_length(char s[])

It must fill the interval dp table (growing substring length; equal ends add 2 to the inner interval, otherwise take the better drop) and return dp[0][|s|-1].

Input Format:
Line 1: the string (no spaces).

Output Format:
One line with the LPS length.

Constraints:
1 <= |s| <= 50, string uses letters/digits only

questions.title: Frog Jump Energy
questions.description:
A frog crosses stones 1..n; from stone i it may jump to i+1 or i+2, spending energy equal to the ABSOLUTE height difference between the stones. Minimise the total energy from stone 1 to stone n with a dp table: dp[i] = min(dp[i-1] + |h[i]-h[i-1]|, dp[i-2] + |h[i]-h[i-2]|).

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int frog_min_cost(int n, int h[])

It must fill dp bottom-up (dp[0] = 0) and return dp[n-1].

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n stone heights.

Output Format:
One line with the minimum total energy.

Constraints:
2 <= n <= 5000, 1 <= h[i] <= 10000

questions.title: Paint House Cost
questions.description:
A row of n houses must be painted, each in one of 3 colours (costs cost[i][0..2]); adjacent houses may NOT share a colour. Minimise the total cost with a dp over houses tracking the best cost ending in each colour: new_r = cost[i][0] + min(g, b) and so on.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int min_paint_cost(int n, int cost[][3])

It must roll three running values r, g, b through the houses and return the smallest of the final three.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Then n lines, each with 3 integers (red, green, blue costs of that house).

Output Format:
One line with the minimum total painting cost.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 1 <= cost[i][c] <= 1000

questions.title: Longest Increasing Run
questions.description:
A data pipeline keeps its records stable when their values form a LONGEST STRICTLY INCREASING SUBSEQUENCE (order preserved, each picked value strictly larger than the last). Find that length with the classic O(n^2) dp: dp[i] = 1 + max(dp[j] over j < i with a[j] < a[i]).

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int lis_length(int n, int a[])

It must fill the dp table and return the maximum dp[i].

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n values.

Output Format:
One line with the LIS length.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 2000, |a[i]| <= 1000000000

questions.title: Grid Route Counter
questions.description:
A courier walks an R x C city grid moving only RIGHT or DOWN from the top-left to the bottom-right corner. Count the DISTINCT routes with a dp table where dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j] + dp[i][j-1] (border cells have exactly 1 route). The count can exceed int — use long long.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long grid_paths(int R, int C)

It must fill the dp table and return dp[R-1][C-1].

Input Format:
Line 1: R and C.

Output Format:
One line with the number of distinct routes.

Constraints:
1 <= R, C <= 15

questions.title: Terrain Lowest Cost Path
questions.description:
A survey drone crosses an R x C terrain grid moving only RIGHT or DOWN; entering cell (i, j) costs g[i][j] (the start cell counts). Minimise the total path cost with a dp table: dp[i][j] = g[i][j] + min(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1]). The scaffold defines MAXG as 100 and stores the R x C grid in g row by row (R rows, C columns of integers).

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int min_path_sum(int R, int C, int g[][MAXG])

It must fill a dp table and return dp[R-1][C-1].

Input Format:
Line 1: R and C. Then R lines with C integers each.

Output Format:
One line with the minimum path cost.

Constraints:
1 <= R, C <= 100, 0 <= g[i][j] <= 1000

questions.title: Subset Sum Tallies
questions.description:
An inventory counts HOW MANY subsets of the n items sum exactly to target (items are used at most once each; items are distinguished by position). Fill a dp table over sums: dp[0] = 1, and processing each item iterate sums DOWNWARDS with dp[s] += dp[s - a[i]] so every item contributes at most once.

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int count_subsets(int n, int a[], int target)

It must fill the dp table and return dp[target].

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n item values. Line 3: target.

Output Format:
One line with the number of subsets.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 20, 1 <= a[i] <= 100, 1 <= target <= 2000
